## First market: microschools in Idaho and Utah {#first-market}

<span class="kicker">Go-to-market · the working default</span>

<div class="cards">
<div class="card"><strong>Who first</strong>Microschools and small private schools, about 10 to 150 families, that bill through Stripe. Families in state education programs need payment records that hold up.</div>
<div class="card card--green"><strong>How it spreads</strong>
<ul>
<li>Every receipt will carry a "Verify at trifold…" link</li>
<li>Platforms that adopt the receipt format extend the verifier's reach</li>
<li>CPAs bring clients; their seats will be free</li>
</ul></div>
<div class="card card--ink"><strong>Then</strong>Businesses with the same shape (memberships, credits, bookings): studios, tutoring, camps, gyms. Vertical software embeds Trifold.</div>
</div>

<p class="assume-note"><span class="tag tag--assume">Assumption</span> Idaho and Utah first is the working default, still an open decision. Phase 1 target (months 3–9): 100 schools on the hosted service, 20 paying, about 10 CPA partners.</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/business/business-plan.md` §1 (first market), §4 (customers: 10–150 families, Stripe, Idaho and Utah; next: studios, tutoring, camps, gyms; channels) and §7 (the three growth loops; the phase table, phase 1 "proof it worked": 100 schools on cloud, 20 paying, ~10 CPA partners). Why Idaho and Utah: `docs/business/market-research.md` §4 (related-party design partners, B4 Uni and buzz-school, not independent customers; state programs such as Idaho's parental choice tax credit and Utah Fits All; "check each program's current receipt rules before building on this").

Phase 1 numbers are targets in a draft plan, not results. First market is "the working default" (business-plan §1 and §12 item 3, audited 2026-11-07). The "Verify at trifold…" link appears once schools issue receipts; none does yet (business-plan §3).
:::
